properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: werkzeug 2.3.8 declared (requirements.txt:97); its werkzeug.security module ships PBKDF2 (pbkdf2:sha256) and scrypt password hashing. First-party code imports only werkzeug.utils.secure_filename (non-crypto), so this is a shipped-capability entry — the library is present in the build regardless of use; presence is what the inventory records. Changeable here (upgrade/pin).

components.name: Python ssl sessions on default settings (OpenSSL version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS transport asset: requests 2.31.0 (+urllib3 2.0.7, LIB-2dbdc8e2) is used for live outbound HTTPS — gworkspace/mail.py, addons/*, agentmemory (plus 4 requests call sites the collector missed, reported as findings). Default TLS key exchange is ECDHE over the runtime OpenSSL — quantum-unsafe, harvest-now-decrypt-later. PQ capability depends on the runtime OpenSSL (≥3.5 offers X25519MLKEM768); the tree doesn't pin one. Changeable here by pinning a runtime with hybrid KEX.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JOSE capability entry for python-jose 3.3.0 (declared with the [cryptography] extra, requirements.txt:107): provides JWS/JWT sign+verify (HS256/RS256/ES256) and JWE (RSA-OAEP/AES-GCM) — all quantum-unsafe algorithms. No first-party call site found (no jose/jwt imports in app code) — capability ships in the build regardless; recorded as available. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provider facet of the python-jose dependency — the JOSE capability it supplies is recorded separately in ALG-386b2ee4; both stem from requirements.txt:107. Version 3.3.0 offers no PQ algorithms.
